scope: Route metadata and publication-surface readiness; not an expert certification of runnable conditions
importantLimitations: The route-safety audit is a structural completeness check. It does not validate paddler competency, current wood, local rescue capacity, closures, or whether a threshold remains safe after a rapid changes character.
A gauge reading is an observation and planning input, not a runnable guarantee. Proxy gauges add reach-mismatch uncertainty, and even direct gauges do not replace same-day visual scouting.

American Whitewater's safety guidance treats Class IV as requiring scouting and practiced rescue capability, and Class V as requiring extensive experience, reliable self-rescue, and practiced rescue skills.

publicationExposure.currentIssue: The catalog-wide publication gate now keeps all Idaho Class IV+ routes out of the scored same-day route surface; high-consequence routes remain planning-only or withheld.
existingControls: Planning routes show a planning status and no same-day score.
Proxy routes are not score-eligible unless explicitly authored as planning routes.
Scored routes expose the advanced safety label, hazard chips, safety notes, threshold source, gauge freshness, and access/logistics sections.

recommendation.decision: Do not launch all Idaho rapid classes into one undifferentiated same-day scoring catalog.

stagedPolicy.classIToIII: Eligible for live scoring only when the route has a reach-matched direct/official gauge, current access and closure controls, and reviewed safety metadata.
stagedPolicy.classIV: Planning/expert-only by default. Consider live scoring only after route-specific expert review confirms direct telemetry, current access, scout/portage/rescue information, and an explicit competency warning.
stagedPolicy.classVAndVPlus: Planning-only. Keep thresholds as planning cues, but do not present a same-day paddle/no-paddle score or alert as if the gauge can certify safety.

recommendation.nextGate: Any future Class IV+ live-scoring exception would require a separately approved expert-publication policy, route-specific competency/rescue sign-off, and a regression test; the default remains planning-only or withheld.
